KR.read: Korea's sun-care segment now has a domestic anchor, but the cleanest figure is a production measure, not a retail one: MFDS sunscreen production value of KRW 0.47tn for CY2025 (MEDIUM confidence, PRODUCTION basis), which is factory-gate output and must not be read as domestic retail sell-through. Retail-basis market sizes are two conflicting LOW-confidence aggregator estimates — Grand View US$330mn (2024) versus MarkNtel US$747mn (2025), roughly a 2.3x spread. Reported SPF penetration is high but also conflicting (45% to 75%, both LOW).
KR.trend: MFDS production grew +9.4% YoY in CY2025 (observed, MEDIUM, PRODUCTION basis). Forecast retail CAGRs sit between 3.59% (MarkNtel) and 8.3% (Grand View), both LOW. A separately reported +43% figure (Samsung Securities via Korea Herald) is a 2025 projection tied to overseas/e-commerce sales, not domestic retail growth.
KR.caveats: The strongest figure (MFDS) is on a PRODUCTION basis and is not comparable to retail sizes; the two retail estimates are LOW-confidence aggregator numbers about 2.3x apart, so absolute domestic scale remains uncertain.

IN.read: India sun care sizes at roughly US$0.58bn (IMARC, 2025) to US$0.89bn (TechSci, 2024) on a RETAIL basis, both LOW confidence — and these are effectively sunscreen-only sizings, which the segment-level figure already on file was built from. Sub-segment sun_protection now carries its own explicit sizings from the same houses, plus a MEDIUM-confidence K-beauty shelf-price point (Beauty of Joseon, Rs1570 MRP, [CORRIDOR]-tagged).
IN.trend: Forecast CAGRs cluster 6.0-6.8% (IMARC, TechSci; LOW). The eye-catching +170% (2026) and +85% (2023) growth figures are quick-commerce channel and Nykaa-platform reads respectively (LOW/MEDIUM), not whole-segment growth — the category is surging on q-commerce off a small base, which is not the same as the segment growing that fast.
IN.caveats: Every size figure is a LOW aggregator estimate with a wide (~1.5x) spread and a sunscreen-only definition; the high growth numbers are channel-specific, not segment-wide, and must not be read as the market's overall rate.

combined.read: Both geographies now carry RETAIL value_usd_bn figures, so a directional size comparison is possible: India's sunscreen market (~US$0.58-0.89bn) is broadly comparable to, and probably somewhat larger than, Korea's retail sunscreen (~US$0.33-0.75bn) — but every figure on both sides is LOW confidence with a ~2x internal spread, so this is directional only, not a firm ranking. Korea's most reliable datapoint is production (KRW 0.47tn, MEDIUM), a different basis that cannot be set against India's retail figures. On the corridor, sun care is baseline whitespace #2: Nykaa sunscreen grew +85% YoY and Korean-sunscreen searches +148%, evidencing real K-beauty sunscreen pull into India even though no corridor-specific market size exists yet.
